workforce.label: board-certified physicians
workforce.definition: ABMS Medical Genetics and Genomics specialty proxy

need.label: Americans with a rare disease
secondary: About 80% of rare diseases are genetic
need.scope_note: Rare disease is a strategic genomics proxy, not the full population using genetics, pharmacogenomics, cancer genomics, or reproductive testing.
need.source_label: NIH/NCATS Rare Diseases Are Not Rare

funding.scope_note: Lead-institute proxy; genomics is funded throughout NIH, other agencies, health systems, philanthropy, and industry.

digital_leverage.basis: Inherently computational data, rapidly improving standards, reusable variant knowledge, and major opportunities in phenotype capture, interpretation, counseling, and longitudinal reanalysis.

strategy.labor: Build around clinical geneticists, laboratory specialists, and genetic counselors by reducing phenotype capture, evidence review, interpretation, handoff, and reanalysis burden.
strategy.applications: Focus on diagnostic-odyssey shortening, phenotype-to-variant workflows, report comprehension, VRS and FHIR interoperability, and responsible reanalysis rather than sequencing alone.
strategy.group: Genomics is the clearest labor-scarcity and software-leverage signal. Convene clinicians, labs, counselors, rare-disease communities, informaticians, and payers around specific diagnostic pathways.
